newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Rising maize futures dominate trade on Hungary BCE.
newsitem.headline: Rising maize futures dominate trade on Hungary BCE.

text.p: The bulk of the turnover of the Budapest Commodity Exchange (BCE) grain section was made up of maize contracts for July, with maize price rises mirroring wheat price changes, dealers said.
"Maize prices can only have risen as a reaction to wheat price rises as nothing else has changed," said Tamas Kobulniczky of Swap. "The one million tonnes maize surplus did not go down".
Maize prices rose to 20,300 forints, up 400, for the most traded maturity, July.
"July was a lucky (buy and sell) match as apart from this there was hardly any trade," Kobulniczky said.
Milling wheat prices continued a rise which began on Friday on unfounded fears that sleet could endanger the crop, Kobulniczky added.
Market players began speculating on Friday that wheat could rot under the ice cover, but Kobulnicky believed the fear was not justified as temperatures are too low.
"These are just market reactions -- the upward spiralling could continue," he said, adding that nobody was willing to sell as they expect prices to go higher.
"After another two days of rises wheat prices could stabilize," he said.
Milling wheat prices for the 1996 crop ended at 29,060 forints for March and 28,920 for July while 1997 crop prices closed between 21,800 for July to 24,620 for December.
Total turnover was a very light 448 contracts or 180.63 million forints, of which 315 contracts were for July delivery maize.
Lot size is 20,000 kgs for all contracts.
